remaining_uncertainties: Forward citation lists were partially retrievable: Semantic Scholar succeeded for six seeds (KYC 28 citing works, 2512.02902 17, LIBERO-RIG 1, CMA 1, RSB 1, 2610.01626 0). More Structure (2607.09825) returned 429 on every attempt, but OpenAlex reports cited_by=0 and a Google Scholar exact-title lookup shows no 'Cited by' entry, so its citing list is very likely empty; this gap is no longer treated as material.

The surviving candidate C1 was narrowed after a second full-text pass: LIBERO-RIG already defines 'tolerance per axis' (Table 5) and More Structure already demonstrates the mechanism (spatial grounding fixes Near-Miss 31%->2.5% but leaves No-Grasp unchanged). What remains untested is only the cross-task predictive relation, and no pilot evidence exists that same-task/different-failure-mode variants can be constructed.

None of the four papers whose protocols the surviving candidate would reuse (More Structure, LIBERO-RIG, 2610.01626, 2512.02902) contains a project or code URL in its arXiv HTML or PDF, and a GitHub repository search for LIBERO-RIG finds no matching repo. The failure taxonomy and tolerance protocol therefore have to be reimplemented, which is an unverified 1-2 week cost and a feasibility risk rather than a scientific unknown.
40 of 98 registered papers were read at abstract level only (arXiv HTML rate limits); they may contain direct competitors that would change the crowding judgement.
Conference-versus-arXiv version differences were not compared for most entries.
Real-robot evidence in this literature rests on 20-30 trials per condition, which limits the statistical strength of any action-level claim, including future ones.
Whether a measurement/prediction contribution is acceptable as the master's small paper is an advisor judgement that literature research cannot settle.
conclusion: After 130 arXiv queries, six Google Scholar probes and 95 registered papers, four passes and partial forward-citation chasing, five of seven directions fail the hard vetoes. The citation audit strengthened this: about 24 of KYC's 28 citing works are viewpoint or camera-robustness variants (the rest are calibration, action-space grounding and distribution-shift work), and new finds (CAG/LIBERO-CF, paired instruction dependence) further crowd the evidence-use direction. One direction survives only in a narrowed, medium-low-confidence form: whether baseline failure-mode composition plus the intervention's reduction of the operative spatial error predicts the action benefit of a spatial upgrade. Its mechanism is already demonstrated on a single task and per-axis tolerance is already operationalised, so the remaining contribution is a cross-task prediction study whose utility must be shown as selection value, not correlation; a low-cost-hardware benchmark also shows execution instability often dominates, capping the headroom. The report recommends no experiment until seven explicit gates are met, and states that if the predictive relation does not hold, no candidate in this scope qualifies.
